causal_chain: A candidate-conditioned support router can upweight the specific historical items that justify a candidate instead of collapsing the whole history into one static user vector.
A parallel inhibition router can learn which historical items provide counter-evidence for a candidate, separating weak relevance from active mismatch.
Combining direct affinity, routed support, and routed inhibition yields more selective full-sort scores than static embedding matching.

More selective scores should improve ranking of held-out items, especially for users with diverse histories and for candidates that are neither globally popular nor nearest to the user's average taste.
Users with mixed-taste histories contain only a subset of past items that are relevant to any given candidate item.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or extra history aggregation capacity rather than from the distinct support-versus-inhibition routing mechanism.
discriminative_predictions: If the inhibition channel is mechanistically useful, removing only the inhibition route should hurt ranking on hard-candidate contrasts more than removing an equal number of parameters elsewhere.

Relative to a matched mechanism-off control with the same base embeddings and pairwise loss, the routed model should show larger gains for users with longer or more diverse training histories than for users with very short histories.

The routed model should assign higher attention concentration to a small subset of history items for each scored candidate, while the mechanism-off control cannot produce candidate-specific support redistribution.
expected_evidence: A measurable ablation gap between full dual-route scoring and attraction-only scoring, indicating that inhibition is contributing beyond simple history attention.
Improved full-sort NDCG@10 over the matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Per-candidate support weights that vary meaningfully across candidates for the same user rather than collapsing to near-uniform averages.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched control that replaces candidate-conditioned support and inhibition routing with a single uniform or candidate-independent history summary matches or exceeds the proposed model's NDCG@10, the frontier claim is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This is not a parameter tweak of matrix factorization or LightGCN. It introduces a new interaction structure in which each candidate is scored through target-conditioned routing over the user's full training history with separate evidence-for and evidence-against channels. That requires custom history retrieval, dual attention operators, and a new scoring composition unavailable in the current executable profile operators.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that scores each user-item pair through dual target-conditioned routing over the user's training-history items—one route assembling support evidence and one route assembling inhibitory counter-evidence—will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filters because it can distinguish which past interactions specifically justify a candidate from which past interactions argue against it.
implementation_requirements: Compose the final score from direct user-item affinity plus a support term minus an inhibition term, trained with pairwise BPR-style loss.

For a candidate item, compute support attention over the user's interacted items using candidate-to-history compatibility, and compute inhibition attention using a distinct counter-evidence compatibility function.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with train-matrix history lookup for each user.

Include a mechanism-off switch that replaces dual routing with a candidate-independent averaged history summary while preserving the same optimizer, loss family, training loop, and evaluation protocol.
Maintain learnable user embeddings, item embeddings, and separate query/key/value projections for support and inhibition routing.
Provide efficient full-sort scoring by batching candidate items and masking padded history positions without using held-out interactions.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same candidate-local GeneralRecommender scaffold, embedding dimensionality budget, pairwise loss, regularization family, and training/evaluation pipeline, but disable target-conditioned dual routing so scoring depends only on direct affinity plus one candidate-independent pooled history summary.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Replace static user representation scoring with dual target-conditioned history routing: a support router gathers positive collaborative evidence from relevant past items for each candidate, while an inhibition router gathers conflicting evidence and subtracts it during scoring.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is the same model skeleton with identical embeddings and pairwise training, except the support and inhibition routers are removed. The user's history is compressed once into a single candidate-independent pooled vector, and the final score uses only direct affinity plus that pooled-history interaction term.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A two-channel target-aware history-routing recommender where each candidate item attends over a user's train-history items through separate support and inhibition projections, compared against the same architecture with candidate-independent pooled history and no inhibition route.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M full-sort pairwise protocol, does candidate-conditioned dual routing over a user's historical items provide ranking signal beyond what static user embeddings or candidate-independent history pooling can express?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: ML-1M history lengths are moderate enough that batched target-conditioned attention over padded user histories should fit within the stated 10 GPU-minute and 30 wall-minute qualification budget if implemented with sampled pairwise training and vectorized full-sort scoring.
